answer: A way I love to relax is by listening to music while doing absolutely nothing else. It might sound simple, but in our busy lives, giving yourself permission to just be still is something of a [[rarity]]. I usually do this in the evening, after we have had dinner as a family, lying on my bed or sitting on the rooftop of our building with a cup of tea. The rooftop is my favourite spot, because it is quiet up there and on clear nights you can feel a gentle breeze coming off the river. What makes it so relaxing is that it lets my mind completely [[unwind]] after a hectic day. Depending on my mood, I choose calming acoustic tracks or something more uplifting. I never use music as background noise at these times; I give it my full attention, which is what makes the difference. Quite often I end up listening to old Bengali songs that my parents used to play, which feel like home to me. There is something almost [[meditative]] about focusing purely on the music and letting my thoughts settle. Honestly, this small ritual has become essential for my mental wellbeing. In a world that constantly demands our attention, having a way to properly [[decompress]] is genuinely valuable. It costs nothing and asks nothing of me, which is exactly why I love it. I always feel noticeably calmer and more centred afterwards, ready to face whatever comes next, and I think everyone deserves a little [[sanctuary]] like that.

followUps.q: Do you use headphones or play the music aloud?
followUps.answer: Usually headphones, because I don't want to disturb my sister while she's studying. On the rooftop, though, I sometimes play it quietly through my phone, which feels more relaxed and natural.

followUps.q: Have your ways of relaxing changed since you were a child?
followUps.answer: Quite a lot. As a child I relaxed by running around outside with my cousins. Now I need calm rather than excitement, which I suppose is a natural part of growing older.

note: Added family dinner, the rooftop and river breeze, old Bengali songs and a close; plain 'rare' became [[rarity]], added [[sanctuary]].
